sources.title: LangChain

establishes.statement: LangChain/LangGraph give foundational building blocks with basic runtime support for LLM applications.
establishes.support_quote: LangChain and LangGraph Chase (2022) provide foundational building blocks with basic runtime support

sources.title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation Framework

establishes.statement: AutoGen adds Python and bash execution to a conversation framework, but with stateless command execution.
establishes.support_quote: AutoGen advances beyond basic frameworks by implementing Python and bash execution capabilities, though with stateless command execution

sources.title: CrewAI

establishes.statement: CrewAI orchestrates multi-agent communication and offers a sandboxed but limited code-interpreter feature.
establishes.support_quote: CrewAI CrewAI (2024) focuses on orchestrating multi-agent communications ... frameworks like CrewAI offer sandboxed but limited code interpreter features

sources.title: WorkArena: How Capable Are Web Agents at Solving Common Knowledge Work Tasks? (BrowserGym)

establishes.statement: BrowserGym is a Gym-style environment specifically targeting web-browsing capability, and supplies the browser action/observation primitives OpenHands reuses.
establishes.support_quote: BrowserGym ServiceNow specifically targets web browsing capabilities

sources.title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines

establishes.statement: DSPy emphasizes end-to-end prompt optimization rather than execution/runtime.
establishes.support_quote: DSPy Khattab et al. (2024) emphasizes end-to-end prompt optimization

sources.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for a Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
sources.venue: The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations

establishes.statement: MetaGPT emphasizes standardized operating procedures for multi-agent software-development collaboration.
establishes.support_quote: with MetaGPT Hong et al. (2023) emphasizing standardized operating procedures

sources.title: Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs (GPTSwarm)

establishes.statement: GPTSwarm represents agent systems as optimizable graphs (nodes = operations, edges = communication), enabling automatic optimization of multi-agent systems; OpenHands integrates it as one AgentHub agent.
establishes.support_quote: GPTSwarm (Zhuge et al., 2024) pioneers the use of optimizable graphs to construct agent systems, unifying language agent frameworks through modularity

sources.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering

establishes.statement: SWE-Agent shows that a carefully crafted agent-computer interface (ACI) matters for solving complex software-engineering tasks, and reaches 18.0% on SWE-Bench Lite (gpt-4-1106-preview) and 87.7% on HumanEvalFix with a 1-shot demonstration.
establishes.support_quote: SWE-Agent (Yang et al., 2024) highlights the importance of a carefully crafted Agent-Computer Interface (ACI ... ) in successfully solving complex tasks

sources.title: AutoCodeRover: Autonomous Program Improvement

establishes.statement: AutoCodeRover addresses GitHub issues via code search and abstract-syntax-tree manipulation, reaching 19.0% on SWE-Bench Lite (gpt-4-0125-preview).
establishes.support_quote: AutoCodeRover Zhang et al. (2024b) addresses GitHub issues via code search and abstract syntax tree manipulation

sources.title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents

establishes.statement: Agentless reaches 27.3% on SWE-Bench Lite with gpt-4o, the highest of the compared SWE specialist baselines.
establishes.support_quote: Agentless (Xia et al., 2024) gpt-4o 27.3

sources.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
sources.venue: The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations

establishes.statement: SWE-Bench evaluates whether an agent's patch resolves a real GitHub issue, checked against a hidden human-written test suite; SWE-Bench Lite is a 300-instance canonical subset.
establishes.support_quote: SWE-Bench (Jimenez et al., 2024) is designed to assess agents' abilities in solving real-world GitHub issues ... A canonical subset, SWE-bench Lite, is created to facilitate accessible and efficient testing

sources.title: OctoPack: Instruction Tuning Code Large Language Models (HumanEvalFix)

establishes.statement: HumanEvalFix tasks agents with fixing an inserted bug in a function using provided test cases (164 Python instances); OpenHands follows this paper's pass@k evaluation setup.
establishes.support_quote: HumanEvalFix (Muennighoff et al., 2024) tasks agents to fix a bug in a provided function with the help of provided test cases ... We follow the setup from Muennighoff et al. (2024) using pass@k

sources.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
sources.venue: The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations

establishes.statement: WebArena is a self-hostable, execution-based web-agent benchmark with 812 human-curated tasks across shopping, forums, developer platforms, and content-management systems; its own zero-shot-prompted agent scores 14.4% with gpt-4-turbo.
establishes.support_quote: WebArena comprises 812 human-curated task instructions across various domains

sources.title: Reinforcement Learning on Web Interfaces Using Workflow-Guided Exploration (MiniWoB++)

establishes.statement: MiniWoB++ is a suite of 125 synthetic, minimalist web interfaces with built-in reward functions; the paper's own trained Workflow-Guided-Exploration agent scores 34.6% on the full set.
establishes.support_quote: The tasks are synthetically initialized on 125 different minimalist web interfaces

sources.title: A Data-Driven Approach for Learning to Control Computers (CC-Net)

establishes.statement: CC-Net is a specialist model trained with reinforcement learning plus human-annotated behavioral cloning; on MiniWoB++ it reaches 91.1%, well above every LLM-prompted agent OpenHands compares against.
establishes.support_quote: CC-NET (Humphreys et al., 2022) Trained specialist model with RL and human annotated BC

sources.title: GAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants

establishes.statement: GAIA consists of 466 curated real-world tasks across three difficulty levels, requiring reasoning, multi-modal understanding, web browsing, and coding.
establishes.support_quote: GAIA consists of 466 curated tasks across three levels

sources.title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark

establishes.statement: GPQA measures graduate-level, 'Google-proof' question answering; the paper reports expert-human accuracy of 81.3% and non-expert-human accuracy of 21.9% on the diamond set.
establishes.support_quote: GPQA (Rein et al., 2023) evaluates agents' ability for coordinated tool use when solving challenging graduate-level problems

sources.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents

establishes.statement: AgentBench's OS (bash) subset (144 tasks) requires multi-turn reasoning and decision-making via direct bash interaction with a task-specific operating system.
establishes.support_quote: AgentBench (Liu et al., 2023) evaluates agents' reasoning and decision-making abilities in a multi-turn, open-ended generation setting. We selected the code-grounded operating system (OS) subset with 144 tasks

sources.title: MINT: Evaluating LLMs in Multi-Turn Interaction with Tools and Language Feedback

establishes.statement: MINT tests multi-turn tool use with GPT-4-simulated natural-language feedback, up to five interaction rounds with two solution attempts, on math and code subsets.
establishes.support_quote: MINT (Wang et al., 2024b) is a benchmark designed to evaluate agents' ability to solve challenging tasks through multi-turn interactions using tools and natural language feedback simulated by GPT-4

sources.title: ProofWriter: Generating Implications, Proofs, and Abductive Statements over Natural Language
sources.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL-IJCNLP 2021

establishes.statement: ProofWriter is a synthetic deductive-reasoning dataset; OpenHands focuses on its hardest, 5-hop subset (600 instances).
establishes.support_quote: ProofWriter (Tafjord et al., 2021) is a synthetic dataset created to assess deductive reasoning abilities of LLMs ... we focus on the most challenging subset, which contains 600 instances requiring 5-hop reasoning

sources.title: Logic-LM: Empowering Large Language Models with Symbolic Solvers for Faithful Logical Reasoning

establishes.statement: Logic-LM pairs an LLM with a symbolic solver, reaching 79.6% on ProofWriter's 5-hop subset with gpt-4; OpenHands reuses its logical-form parses to reduce semantic-parsing error.
establishes.support_quote: Logic-LM (Pan et al., 2023) ... To minimize the impact of potential errors in semantic parsing, we use the logical forms provided by Logic-LM

sources.title: Probing the Multi-Turn Planning Capabilities of LLMs via 20 Question Games (Entity Deduction Arena)

establishes.statement: Entity Deduction Arena has agents deduce an unknown entity via strategic questioning (20-Questions-style), testing state tracking, planning, and inductive reasoning over multi-turn dialogue.
establishes.support_quote: Entity Deduction Arena (EDA) (Zhang et al., 2024a) evaluates agents' ability to deduce unknown entities through strategic questioning, akin to the 20 Questions game

sources.title: Executable Code Actions Elicit Better LLM Agents (CodeAct)

establishes.statement: CodeAct is the framework behind OpenHands' default CodeActAgent and behind the design rationale that a code/PL-based action space is a comprehensive, flexible, reliable, and maintainable set of primitives.
establishes.support_quote: Inspired by CodeAct (Wang et al., 2024a), OpenHands connects an agent with the environment through a core set of general actions

sources.title: Auto-GPT: An Autonomous GPT-4 Experiment

establishes.statement: AutoGPT decomposes a user goal into executable steps; on GAIA's L1 validation set it scores 13.2% with gpt-4-turbo.
establishes.support_quote: Notable works such as Auto-GPT Gravitas (2023) harness LLMs for task completion by decomposing user goals into executable steps

sources.title: Communicative Agents for Software Development (ChatDev)

establishes.statement: ChatDev automates the software-development lifecycle in a pattern resembling the waterfall model.
establishes.support_quote: Innovations such as ChatDev Qian et al. (2023) automate the software development lifecycle akin to the waterfall model

sources.title: AgentCoder: Multi-Agent-based Code Generation with Iterative Testing and Optimisation

establishes.statement: AgentCoder iteratively refines code generation with integrated testing and feedback.
establishes.support_quote: AgentCoder Huang et al. (2024) iteratively refines code generation with integrated testing and feedback

sources.title: Lemur: Harmonizing Natural Language and Code for Language Agents

establishes.statement: Lemur-chat-70b, evaluated zero-shot on WebArena, scores 5.3%.
establishes.support_quote: Lemur (Xu et al., 2023) Lemur-chat-70b

sources.title: Large Language Models Can Self-Improve at Web Agent Tasks

establishes.statement: A 72B model trained with self-improvement synthetic data reaches 9.4% on WebArena.
establishes.support_quote: Patel et al. (2024) Trained 72B with self-improvement synthetic data

sources.title: AutoWebGLM: Bootstrap and Reinforce a Large Language Model-based Web Navigating Agent

establishes.statement: A 7B model trained with human/agent hybrid annotation reaches 18.2% on WebArena, the strongest trained specialist compared in the table.
establishes.support_quote: AutoWebGLM (Lai et al., 2024) Trained 7B with human/agent hybrid annotation

sources.title: Autonomous Evaluation and Refinement of Digital Agents (Auto Eval & Refine)

establishes.statement: GPT-4 with a Reflexion-style retry loop and a GPT-4V-based completion reward model reaches 20.2% on WebArena, the highest baseline OpenHands compares against there; the authors plan to attach this approach to their own browsing agent as an optional component.
establishes.support_quote: Auto Eval & Refine Pan et al. (2024), an agent retry-on-error strategy with Reflexion Shinn et al. (2024) prompts and task completion reward models, will be integrated as an optional component attached to our browsing agent
